PERMITS AND LICENSES COMMITTEE
  MINUTES
  May 23, 2019

A meeting of the Permits and License Committee was held on Thursday, May 23, 2019,
at 2:00 pm in the Community Room “A”, 1st Floor.

Roll Call:  Members Present:  Harjinder Singh, Administration
  Aisha Thompson, City Clerk
  Lt. David Salcedo, Police Department
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Planning & Building Department

  Staff Present:  Peggy L. Velasquez, Finance Department

Also present: Arrick Turner, Supervisor of Darby Park and Jerry Tucker, Manager of
Code Enforcement.

Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items
During public comments any person may address the Permits & License Committee,
provided the item is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Permits & License
Committee.
Chairman Singh asked if there were any persons present who wished to address the
Permits & License Committee on any item on the Agenda.
Chairman Singh reported that there were no public requests to speak.

Agenda Items

A motion was moved and seconded to approve the minutes from the meeting held on
May 9, 2018, Motion carried approved, Lt. Salcedo abstained.

Permit Request(s):

Item #1:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  Robert Mines to host an Inglewood Juneteenth Celebration at Darby Park,
  June 15, 2019, from 10:00 am – 3:00 pm. Approval for one day event at
  Darby Park subject to; applicant responsible to monitor crowd control;
  maintain and keep event area clean during and after event; no gang
  paraphernalia exhibited and no gang attire to be worn; No Police staffing
  will be required, however, APPLICANT AND/OR EMPLOYEES OR
  GUESTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE ACTIVE PARTICIPANTS IN CALLING
  POLICE FOR POLICE RELATED, UNUSUAL, ILLEGAL, AND/OR
  ACTIVITY THAT MAY NECESSITATE A POLICE RESPONSE OR
  RESPONSE FROM OTHER CITY GOVERNMENT SERVICES (I.E. CODE
  ENFORCEMENT, PLANNING, FINANCE, ETC.). NO USE OF
  CANNABIS/MARIJUANA PRODUCTS AND NO SMOKING IN PARK;
  ensure safe pedestrian and vehicular circulation on/off site; adhere to all
  applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including noise
  and signage, local, state and federal laws. (Activity No. 00275338)
 Permits & License Committee  May 23, 2019
Minutes  Page 2 of 6

Item #2:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  Nick Bachman DBA Three Weavers Brewing Company to host a LA Beer
  Week Celebration at 1031 W. Manchester Blvd., Unit A-B, June 23, 2019,
  from 1:00 pm – 5:00 pm.; Approval for one day event within
  industrial/commercial parking lot subject to notify other business within
  shopping center about parking lot; monitor crowd control; maintain and
  keep event area clean during and after event; Provide the Police
  Department a list of entertainers and or DJ’s 5 days prior to event; hire 4
  uniformed security guards registered with the City; must wear security
  marked uniforms; copy of temporary ABC license shall be forwarded to
  Police Department; Concert/DJ area will be fenced off to general public; all
  minors shall be accompanied by parent/adult; minors shall not be in
  possession of or consuming any alcoholic beverages; alcoholic
  beverages/drinks will be in plastic cups outside of business doors, no
  bottles or cans; Applicant shall not sell alcoholic beverages to individual
  who is obviously impaired; No drug use at event. Food trucks shall have
  permit to operate in Inglewood. Advise neighboring businesses of event at
  least 5 days prior; Must adhere to all state and local laws including
  Inglewood Municipal codes; Comply with all IMC Noise standards; All
  Inglewood registered food trucks are to have a LA County Health permit or
  event permit on-site and available for inspection by any Code Enforcement
  Officer or Police Officer. (Activity No. 00275328)

Item #3:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  Rick Miller DBA Inglewood Park Cemetery to host a Jazz Concert – Tribute
  to Gospel at 720 E. Florence Ave., May 26, 2019, from 2:00 pm – 4:00 pm.
  Subject to Inglewood Park Cemetery to provide adequate security
  (minimum 4 + Supervisor) to maintain and monitor crowd control; any
  person directing traffic is required to wear highly-visible retro-reflective
  vests and use flashlights during hours of darkness/dusk; maintain a clear
  access for fire trucks and emergency services; maintain site at all times,
  ensuring site is properly cleaned immediately at the end of the event;
  ensure safe pedestrian and vehicular circulation on/off site; and adhere to
  all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including
  noise and signage, local, state and federal laws. (Activity No. 00275342)

Item #4:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  Kathrine Flory DBA Morningside Unite Church of Christ to conduct a
  Parking Lot Sale at 8722 Crenshaw Blvd., July 13-14, 2019, from 9:00 am
  – 6:00 pm. Subject to applicant responsible for crowd control and event
  clean up. Subject to all applicable IMC regulations; No PD staff required;
  Subjects in parking lot controlling traffic must wear a reflective vest, a flash
  light is required during hours of darkness/dusk; No traffic control on public
  streets; and If parking will consist of street parking, must notify residents of
  event 5 days prior and adhere to all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code
  rules and regulations, including noise and signage, local, state and federal
  laws. (Activity No. 00275248)
 Permits & License Committee  May 23, 2019
Minutes  Page 3 of 6

Item #5:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  Ratha Harntha DBA IMG to host a Fortnite Block Party at the Forum -
  Kareem Lot, June 15, 2019, from 2:00 pm – 8:00 pm. and June 16, 2019,
  from 2:00 pm to 8:00 pm subject to Applicant responsible for crowd control
  and event clean up; Police staffing 6 officers + 1 Sgt. provided by Forum;
  fans shall be directed (by employees) not to point or use/fire simulated
  firearms (nerf guns, bright yellow color) at security, police, or other people;
  only point weapons at targets in the simulated game and/or designated
  players; must have safety zone and security guards monitoring at any
  event/games which include person to person contact or with simulated
  weapons; any simulated weapons must be clearly designated as toys by
  bright colors, nor dark/black color simulated handguns/rifles/firearms
  without approval from PD; no sharp objects; applicant to pay associate
  costs for two (2) assigned Code Enforcement Officers for Noise Mitigation
  and Catering Truck Inspection; contact Code Enforcement Division
  (310.412.5590) and arrange for sound check prior to the start of the event;
  applicant to provide contact information for responsible sound technician;
  applicant and agents are to comply with City's Noise Ordinance (IMC 5-30)
  at all times; applicant and agents are to adhere to permitted start / end
  times; applicant to insure catering truck / ice cream truck is in possession
  of a LA County Health Permit (Subject to on-site inspection) and adhere to
  all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including
  noise and signage, local, state and federal laws. . (Activity No. 00275055)

Item #6:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the permit request for
  City of Inglewood to host the City of Inglewood’s 71st Annual Memorial Day
  Celebration, at Inglewood City Hall – South Lawn Area, May 27, 2019, from
  11:00 am – 1:30 pm, subject to Police Department to provide extra patrol
  as needed due to PD staff will be guests/attending. Have police vehicle
  parked in front on Manchester Blvd. in front (south of) stage for security
  visibility. Provide list of dignitaries and any invited media to PD as soon as
  possible but no less than 3 days prior to event. No drone use without prior
  approval from PD and LAX-FAA. Applicant responsible for crowd control
  and event clean up. Subject to all applicable IMC regulations. (Activity No.
  00275339)

Business License Request(s):

Item #7:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the Business License
  request for Damien Rivera DBA Champion Cutz to operate a Hair Salon at
  10306 S. Prairie Avenue. Payment of annual business license and tax fees;
  Business owner must possess and maintain valid and current
  Establishment License from the State Board of Barbering & Cosmetology;
  Cosmetologist's, Barbers, Esthetician's and Manicurists operating within
  the establishment must possess applicable licenses from the State Board
  of Barbering & Cosmetology; Cosmetologist's, Barbers, Esthetician's and
  Manicurists operating within the establishment is required to register and
  file business tax with the City; Business owner shall provide valid and
  current government-issued identification and copies of applicable state
  licensing on all employee(s) and/or any person operating within the
 Permits & License Committee  May 23, 2019
Minutes  Page 4 of 6

  establishment to the Finance Department; Parties, social events or
  gatherings of any type is strictly prohibited; shall apply/submit application
  for permit for other social/party events. Consumption of alcoholic
  beverages, narcotic drug use (including cannabis activity) is not permitted
  on the premises; Massage therapy of any part of the body is not permitted;
  Adhere to all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations,
  including noise and signage, local, state and federal laws. APPLICANT
  AND EMPLOYEES ARE EXPECTED TO BE ACTIVE PARTICIPANTS IN
  CALLING POLICE FOR POLICE RELATED, UNUSUAL, ILLEGAL,
  AND/OR ACTIVTY THAT MAY NECESSITATE A POLICE RESPONSE
  OR RESPONSE FROM OTHER CITY GOVERNMENT SERVICES (I.E.
  CODE ENFORCEMENT, PLANNING, FINANCE, ETC.) Failure to comply
  with any of the aforementioned will result in the revocation of your business
  license and any future business license application requests. (Activity No.
  00275264)

Item #8:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the Business License
  request for Simply Hybrid LLC DBA Simply Rent A Car: Simply Rent A Car
  to operate at 411 Isis Avenue. (Activity No. 00274990) Approval for office
  use only for car rental business; applicant must provide proof of one year
  lease with option to renew for all vehicles; no parking or storing vehicles or
  inventory on site or on any public right of way; subject to inspection by any
  Code Enforcement Officer or Police Officer; all applicant/employees/agent
  must be in possession of government identification during business
  operation and shall present it at the request of any city official. Adhere to
  all applicable IMC regulations and all State and Federal Laws.

Item #9:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the Business License
  request for AAA Auto Leasing DBA One Stop Classics: One Stop Classics
  to operate at 411 Isis Avenue. (Activity No. 00274992) Approval for office
  use only for car rental business; applicant must provide proof of one year
  lease with option to renew for all vehicles; no parking or storing vehicles or
  inventory on site or on any public right of way; subject to inspection by any
  Code Enforcement Officer or Police Officer; all applicant/employees/agent
  must be in possession of government identification during business
  operation and shall present it at the request of any city official. Adhere to
  all applicable IMC regulations and all State and Federal Laws.

Tobacco Retailer License Request(s):

  Item #10:  A motion was moved and seconded to APPROVE the Tobacco
  Retailer License request for Maebel A. Mubarek DBA ASAP
  Tobacco Shop: ASAP Tobacco Shop to operate as tobacco retailer
  at 211 E. Nutwood Street. (Activity No. 00274751) subject to sales
  of single cigarettes is strictly prohibited; sales of tobacco, hookah,
  vapor and e-cigarette products to minors, under age 21 is strictly
  prohibited; persons purchasing tobacco or any related tobacco
  products shall have valid identification on their person at all times
  to enforce laws restricting underage access to tobacco use,
 Permits & License Committee  May 23, 2019
Minutes  Page 5 of 6

  including hookah products;  “NO LOITERING,” “NO
  TRESSPASSING,” and “NO PANHANDLING” signage must be
  posted outside of the business; sales of marijuana and cannabis
  products, narcotics and narcotics paraphernalia, i.e., any type of
  pipe used to ingest other narcotics such as base “crack” cocaine,
  methamphetamine, including glass cylindrical tube and bubble
  shaped pipes used to smoke and/or ingest narcotics; sales of
  Tobacco pipes is permitted; sales or display of any type of
  weapons, i.e., clubs, swords, knives, pepper spray, Taser/Stun
  guns is strictly prohibited; Tobacco Retailer business owners and/or
  new applicants or their designees is subject to random Permits &
  Licensing establishment inspections at any time of the day or night
  by any Police and Code Enforcement officers; purpose of random
  inspections is to enforce business establishments adhere to the
  regulations set forth by the City of Inglewood and for Community
  Public Health & Safety; parties, social events or gatherings of any
  type is strictly prohibited; music boxes, live bands/music, disc
  jockeys (DJ’s), etc., is strictly prohibited; business owner(s) is
  required to operate within normal business hours; adhere to all
  applicable IMC rules and regulations, including noise and signage.
  Motion carried unanimously.
